title: AMPlify prioritizes bullfrog-genome antimicrobial peptides active against priority pathogens
summary: Researchers integrated the attentive deep-learning classifier AMPlify into a genome-mining pipeline for North American bullfrog sequences. Of 101 candidate mature peptides generated from genome-annotated precursors, AMPlify predicted 75 as antimicrobial; 11 candidates were synthesized and tested, with four showing activity against tested bacteria, including a multidrug-resistant carbapenemase-producing E. coli isolate.
ai_technology: AMPlify, an attentive deep-learning antimicrobial-peptide sequence classifier
organization: Canada's Michael Smith Genome Sciences Centre, BC Cancer; University of British Columbia; University of Victoria; British Columbia Centre for Disease Control; Vancouver General Hospital; University of Washington

evidence.tested: Of 101 candidate mature peptides generated from genome-annotated precursors, AMPlify predicted 75 as antimicrobial; 11 candidates were synthesized and tested, with four showing activity against tested bacteria, including a multidrug-resistant carbapenemase-producing E. coli isolate.
evidence.unknown: This is a small selected validation set: 11 of 75 model-predicted candidates were tested and four were active. Results are in vitro and do not establish therapeutic efficacy or safety. Candidate precursor identification also used homology/genome annotation; attribute AMPlify specifically to mature-peptide prioritization, not the whole discovery workflow.
evidence.ai_role: After bioinformatics identified candidate peptide precursors from the bullfrog genome, AMPlify scored 101 mature peptide sequences and nominated putative AMPs. The team selected 11 predicted peptides for synthesis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing; four showed activity against one or more of six tested bacterial strains, including the carbapenemase-producing E. coli clinical isolate.
